title: Natural coordinates for finite free internal scalar extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small site with the sheafification and closed symmetric monoidal tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] for abelian sheaves. Let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects, and use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and scalar extension and restriction [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Suppose given an $R$-module isomorphism $\theta:R^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi B$, for an integer $n\geq0$, with inverse coordinates $q_i:B\to R$. Write $b_i$ for the image of $1$ under the $i$th basis map $R\to B$ (and its restriction on each test object). There is a natural isomorphism of $R$-module valued functors
$$\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\bigl(B\otimes_R-\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}(-)^n.$$
For an $R$-module sheaf $M$, it and its inverse are specified on local elementary tensors and tuples by
$$\Phi_M(s\otimes m)=(q_i(s)m)_i,\qquad \Psi_M((m_i)_i)=\sum_i b_i\otimes m_i.$$
These formulas specify sheaf morphisms through the tensor and coequalizer universal properties; no equality of tensor-sheaf sections with sectionwise tensor products is asserted.

proof.text: Use sfbSheafTensor_properties to obtain closedness and preservation of small colimits on both sides for the canonical sheaf tensor. Closedness and the abelian structure give MonoidalPreadditive by sfbSheafTensor_monoidalPreadditive; the abelian sheaf category has coequalizers. Introduce arbitrary instances of these Prop-valued consequences as required by FiniteFreeScalarCoordinates.

proof.text: Write N = Res_phi(regular B). Commutativity of B and naturality of the braiding identify its induced right R-action with B tensor phi followed by multiplication. Thus the coequalizers defining Res_phi(extendScalars phi M) and N tensor_R M have the same parallel arrows. Descend their canonical projections in both directions. Cancellation of these epimorphisms proves the inverse identities. After precomposing with R tensor extendPi, the induced action formulas prove R-linearity. This constructs scalarTensorIso, with extendPi followed by its forward map equal to tensorObjPi, and tensorObjPi followed by its inverse equal to extendPi.

proof.text: Tensor theta inverse on the right by M, distribute tensor over the finite biproduct by Mathlib rightDistributor, apply the relative left unitor on each summand, and identify the biproduct with the finite product. Compose with scalarTensorIso. These actual isomorphisms construct finiteCoordinateIso; their inverse identities supply both composite identities without a separate sectionwise tensor calculation.

proof.text: Project this composite to coordinate i. Mathlib rightDistributor_hom_comp_biproduct_pi and biproduct.map_pi give scalarTensorIso.hom followed by (theta.inv followed by pi_i) tensor M and the relative left unitor. The relative left unitor composed after tensorObjPi is the module action, by the bimodule coequalizer description. Precomposing with extendPi therefore gives exactly the asserted forward formula.

proof.text: Expand the inverse of rightDistributor by Mathlib rightDistributor_inv. Transporting this finite sum through the product comparison and the summand unitors gives the sum of pi_i followed by the relative inverse left unitor, (iota_i followed by theta.hom) tensor M, and scalarTensorIso.inv. The relative inverse left unitor is ambient inverse left unitor followed by eta_R tensor M and tensorObjPi: compose with the relative left unitor to verify it using the module unit axiom. The inverse projection identity for scalarTensorIso gives exactly the asserted tuple formula after applying the additive forgetful functor.

proof.text: Check naturality of scalarTensorIso after precomposing with extendPi, using extendPi_extendScalarsMap and tensorObjPi_whiskerLeft. Check finiteCoordinateIso naturality after every finite-product projection; the coordinate formula reduces it to this comparison naturality, whisker_exchange and naturality of the left unitor. NatIso.ofComponents now supplies the natural isomorphism. The finite biproduct/distributor identities include the empty Fin 0 case, so the same construction and empty-sum formulas prove rank zero with no positivity hypothesis.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NM-1c6aff79a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the full statements of the three cited definition nodes (sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars) and the source, the last sentence of lem-sfb-subfield-flat.proof.md in blueprint main-20261015 ('F_X ⊗_{E_X} M ≅ M^n naturally'). The statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint fields are unchanged from the record Q43 created; only split-owned fields changed. There are no new nodes, no repair note for this item, it is not on the route-pivot dropped list, and it cites no SGA. Step 1 gets the Kronecker identity q_i e_j=δ and s=Σφ(q_i s)b_i from θ's two inverse identities and R-linearity of e_i, q_i under the Res action. Step 2 builds Φ through the presheaf tensor, sheafification and the coequalizer. Its balancing check is correct: q_i(sφ(r))m=q_i(s)(rm) uses that B and R are commutative and the action is associative. Testing on the triple tensor is valid because sheafification is strong monoidal. Step 3 builds t_i=b_i⊗–, which is R-linear by the coequalizer relation. In step 4 the composite ΦΨ is the identity because q_i(b_j)=δ_ij. In step 5, ΨΦ(s⊗m)=s⊗m on elementary tensors, and uniqueness out of the bilinear tensor, the sheafification and the coequalizer gives ΨΦ=id. Step 6 proves naturality from the linearity of f. Every step is truly elementary from the cited statements. I tested n=0 (B=0, both sides zero), n=1 with b_1 a unit other than 1, and ordinary modules on a point. No candidate duplicates it: monoidal-finite-free-transport, det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free, scalar-model-finite-flat-resolution and sbc pullback-free-coordinates are all different statements.
